prior_importants.description: After the revert, the skill still asks for prior_importants as {file, line, description, status} and never says how to number entries, while the schema and poster now require {from, index, status} with index counting every element; a model that counts only owed entries makes the poster and metrics resolve the wrong carried important.

priorImportants promises that a misnumbered verdict keeps the important open, but a verdict counted off by the non-owed elements lands on another owed entry and resolves it, dropping a still-open important from the poster's body and the stored record.

findings.description: The prior record is parsed all-or-nothing against today's schema: a pre-#258 record (schema_version 6) whose prior_importants entries lack `description` fails to parse, so the poster carries nothing (not even the record's own findings importants), the body can read "No issues found", and the metrics step records prior_importants: [], losing them for every later round.
findings.body:
**Concern.** `parsePriorReview` checks the whole prior record against today's `priorReviewSchema`. If any one element fails, it returns `null` ([prior-record.utils.ts#L19-L27](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/314272e63219003bff784140082e6d6f76c973f9/tools/review/src/prior-record.utils.ts#L19-L27)):

```ts
export const priorReviewSchema = z.object({
  findings: z.array(findingSchema).nullable(),
  prior_importants: z.array(priorImportantSchema).nullable(),
});
```

([review-metrics.schemas.ts#L240-L244](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/314272e63219003bff784140082e6d6f76c973f9/tools/review/src/review-metrics.schemas.ts#L240-L244))

`priorImportantSchema` requires `description`. That field was added in ab23073 (#258, 2026-11-08). Earlier records store their entries as `{file, line, status}`. Examples on `ci/review-metrics`: `records/42419252161.json` (v6, PR 262) has six such entries, and `records/42419694447.json` has one. A single entry, even a resolved one, is enough to fail the parse. Nothing in the preflight (`priorRecords`, `newestCleanRecord`, `decideMode`) filters on `schema_version`. `priorPath` is also set on full rounds, so the preflight writes that old record to `prior-record.json`.

**Trigger.** An open PR's newest clean record is a v6 round with a non-empty `prior_importants`. The PR then merges main, picking up this code, and gets reviewed.

**Wrong result.**
- `post-review.script.ts` only logs a `::warning::` ([L203-L206](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/314272e63219003bff784140082e6d6f76c973f9/tools/review/src/post-review.script.ts#L203-L206)). Then `priorImportants(null, …)` returns `[]`, which drops the record's own `findings` importants too.
- With a clean round, the body reads "No issues found." and `pr-status.yml` counts zero unthreaded importants.
- `review-metrics.script.ts` writes `prior_importants: []`, so every later round has lost them too.

Before this PR, the model read the record directly, so an old entry shape never went through this parse.

**Fix.** Make the prior-record read accept records written before `description` existed. The writer keeps requiring the field. The `.default` keeps the output type `string`, so `PriorImportant` usage still type-checks. A sturdier option is to parse `findings` and `prior_importants` separately, so one bad array cannot drop the other.

findings.description: This PR rebuilds carried bullets from the prior record, but the pr-status.yml comment at line 116 and ADR 0165 (docs/adr/0165-pr-status-reads-unthreaded-importants-from-the-review-body.md:28-30) still justify letters-and-digits matching because "a carried entry is the model's copy of the prior record"; a maintainer reading either would keep fuzzy matching for drift that can no longer happen.
